Class CoreGraphicsDisplay

java.lang.Object
oshi.driver.common.mac.CoreGraphicsDisplay
@Immutable public final class CoreGraphicsDisplay extends Object
An active display as CoreGraphics reports it, and the logic that matches it to a display enumerated through IOKit.

IOKit enumerates displays with their EDID, and CoreGraphics enumerates them with their mode, but the two share no identifier. CoreGraphics does report the three identity fields of the EDID - CGDisplayVendorNumber, CGDisplayModelNumber and CGDisplaySerialNumber - so a display is matched by comparing those with its EDID. The built-in panel on Apple Silicon has no EDID and is matched by CGDisplayIsBuiltin instead.

Each native backend makes the CoreGraphics calls and builds these; the matching is shared.

    • toMode

      public static DisplayMode toMode(double x, double y, double width, double height, long pixelWidth, long pixelHeight, double refreshRate, double rotation)
      Builds a display's current mode from CoreGraphics values.
      Parameters:
      x - the x origin from CGDisplayBounds, in points
      y - the y origin from CGDisplayBounds, in points
      width - the width from CGDisplayBounds, in points, in the current orientation
      height - the height from CGDisplayBounds, in points, in the current orientation
      pixelWidth - CGDisplayModeGetPixelWidth of the current mode, which is unrotated
      pixelHeight - CGDisplayModeGetPixelHeight of the current mode, which is unrotated
      refreshRate - CGDisplayModeGetRefreshRate of the current mode; 0 for a panel with no fixed rate
      rotation - CGDisplayRotation, in degrees clockwise
      Returns:
      the mode, with the pixel size turned to the current orientation

    • matchEdid

      public static Optional<CoreGraphicsDisplay> matchEdid(List<CoreGraphicsDisplay> displays, byte[] edid)
      Finds the CoreGraphics display that reports the same identity as an EDID.
      Parameters:
      displays - the active CoreGraphics displays
      edid - the EDID of a display enumerated through IOKit
      Returns:
      the one display whose vendor, model and serial numbers match the EDID's, or empty if none do or if more than one does, as happens with two identical monitors that report no serial number
